propositions: Pre-cutover execution traverses explicit intercept/dispatch ladders and policy frozensets in parallel to registry/parser system, preserving a coordination defect that RP-05 must eliminate.

Core top-level execution must move to the selected registry route after pre-operation help boundary, resolving only the lazy handler reference through a closed typed adapter-kind set without re-parsing command/nested options.

Registry-derived mount eligibility, initialization policy (none/init_only/full), confirmation/output extraction, legacy output passthrough, and handler adapter contracts must match all pre-cutover behavioral policies exactly.

Every core canonical command and bridge compatibility spelling must resolve exactly one lazy handler through one of the four closed adapter kinds (dispatcher, argv, argv_tracker, argv_tracker_root), importing only the selected handler/parser modules.

Rollback capability requires derived compatibility exports (policy frozensets) to remain unchanged and reproducible from the live router, with no signature introspection, middleware pipeline, eager parser-tree construction, or second parse added.
